statement: A red-first test can fail for the wrong reason and still look red: the planted-symlink .cejel directory case failed on the old code only because ingest auto-discovery already refused a symlinked <scanned path>/.cejel, so the output write was never reached. That incidental guard vanishes whenever the output directory is not the scanned path's .cejel, as when a subdirectory is scanned from the checkout root, where the old code wrote straight through the link. Assert the refusal message as well as the exit, and add a case that separates the incidental guard from the one under test. Separately, layered defences need one test per layer: with the lstat checks present, deleting O_NOFOLLOW turned no CLI test red, so the open-time layer needed its own direct test.
